Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component.

Test Step 3 of the SFCC-236 build — a small, additive change to an EXISTING, already-shipped, well-tested component: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/{index.tsx,index.test.tsx}`.

## What changed
Added an optional `isLive?: boolean` prop, defaulting to `true`. When explicitly `false`, the component omits `aria-live`/`aria-atomic` entirely (not `aria-live="off"`) on both its loaded and loading/skeleton render branches. Two new tests added; no existing test modified.

## This is a HIGH-STAKES regression-safety step, not a new-feature step
This atom already has a real consumer in production code (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent/index.tsx`, used on the PDP). Your primary job is proving the DEFAULT behaviour (no `isLive` passed) is byte-identical to before this change — any regression here breaks the live PDP.

## Required verification
1. Read the full diff of `index.tsx` — confirm the ONLY changes are: the new prop in the type, the new default in destructuring, and replacing two hardcoded `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` attribute pairs with a spread of a computed object. Confirm nothing else (Was/Now formatting, currency logic, `variant` handling, className/testid, any other prop) was touched, reordered, or renamed.
2. Confirm the existing tests that assert the DEFAULT aria-live behaviour (both loaded and loading branches) still pass UNMODIFIED — read their actual assertions, don't just trust "12 tests passed."
3. Confirm the 2 new tests genuinely test what they claim: `isLive={false}` on the loaded path omits both attributes; `isLive={false}` combined with `isLoading` omits both attributes on the skeleton path too.
4. Confirm the ONE real consumer (`zimmProductContent/index.tsx`) does not pass `isLive` and therefore gets unchanged behaviour — read that call site yourself.
5. Confirm no other file anywhere imports/uses `ZimmProductPrice` that might be affected (grep the whole repo, not just `overrides/`).

## Falsification requirement
Prove the new tests are real, not tautological — break the fix on purpose:
- Temporarily make `isLive` always resolve to rendering both attributes regardless of the prop's value (e.g. hardcode `liveRegionProps` to always include both attrs, ignoring the `isLive` check). Rerun the 2 new tests, confirm BOTH fail. Revert, confirm clean.
- Separately, temporarily make the DEFAULT flip (default `isLive` to `false` instead of `true`, don't change call sites). Rerun the EXISTING default-behaviour tests (the ones asserting aria-live IS present with no prop passed), confirm they fail. This proves those existing tests actually protect the default and aren't just passing by coincidence. Revert, confirm clean.

## Also check
- Does `zimmProductContent`'s own test file need updating, or does it not care about `ZimmProductPrice`'s internal ARIA attributes (i.e., does it mock `ZimmProductPrice` or render it for real)? If it renders it for real and asserts nothing about aria-live, that's fine — just confirm which is the case, don't assume.
- Is the JSDoc added to the new prop accurate and does it match the style/tone of the other props' JSDoc in this file?
- TypeScript: is `liveRegionProps`'s type correctly narrow (literal `'polite'`/`'true'` types, not widened to `string`), matching how the rest of this codebase handles typed ARIA attribute objects?

## Commands to run yourself
```
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent
npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
npm run test
```
Baseline before this step: 49 files / 738 tests should be the claimed new total (up from 736 after Step 2) — verify this exactly and confirm nothing pre-existing regressed.

Report CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE findings, what you falsified, what you could not verify. This step is small — a short, precise report is fine, don't pad it.

content.text:
## Report — SFCC-236 Step 3: `ZimmProductPrice` `isLive` prop

### 1. Compiles and passes — CLEAN

```
npx tsc --noEmit                          → no output, no errors
npx vitest run .../zimmProductPrice       → 12 tests passed (12) — matches 10 existing + 2 new
npx vitest run .../zimmProductContent     → "No test files found" (see Structure angle)
npx eslint .../zimmProductPrice           → no output, no errors
npm run test                              → Test Files 49 passed (49) / Tests 738 passed (738)
```
Baseline claim of 49 files / 738 tests (736+2) is exact, confirmed by real run output, not a summary. `recipeGuards.test.ts` — 6 tests passed, the hard styling gate is clean.

### 2. Tokens — CLEAN for this step, one unrelated pre-existing finding not mine to report

`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` output: 1 unacknowledged violation, `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:20 '59.125em'`. That file is untouched by this step (`git diff --stat` on it is empty) — per the brief, only new unacknowledged findings in touched files are mine to report. `zimmProductPrice/` appears in neither the failing list nor the acknowledged-exception list — genuinely clean. No `var(--zimm-color-*)` tokens were touched by this diff at all (no CSS/styling changed), so the semantic-intent sub-check is vacuous here — dropping it rather than padding with a non-finding.

### 3. Styling conformance — DROPPED (vacuous)

`zimmProductPrice.css.ts` is untouched (`git diff --stat` confirms empty diff). No bare token keys, no new recipe, no interactive pseudo-states introduced — this diff touches zero CSS/styling surface. Nothing to check.

### 4. Structure — CLEAN, one contextual note (not a new finding)

Named export/props-type name unchanged (`ZimmProductPrice` / `ZimmProductPriceProps`). New `isLive?: boolean` follows the optional-with-`?` convention. No new files created. JSDoc on `isLive` is more verbose than the adjacent `isLoading` JSDoc, but it matches this specific file's established register — the file already carries an ~20-line rationale comment above the loaded-branch JSX and an 8-line JSDoc on `currentPrice`. Judged against the *file's* convention rather than just its nearest neighbour, this is consistent, not a deviation.

Contextual note (pre-existing, not introduced by this step): `zimmProductContent/` — the one real consumer — has no `index.test.tsx` at all; its only coverage is `index.stories.tsx` `play` functions (child-count/`rowGap` assertions, confirmed by reading the file). This directly answers the task's "Also check" question: it renders `ZimmProductPrice` for real (not mocked) and asserts nothing about `aria-live`/`aria-atomic`, so it needs no update for this change and isn't a regression risk either way, since it never passes `isLive`.

### 5. Imports — CLEAN, CONFIRMED

No new imports added. Full-repo grep (`grep -rn "ZimmProductPrice"`, not scoped to `overrides/`) surfaces exactly: the component itself, its test, its story, its recipe, its one real JSX consumer (`zimmProductContent/index.tsx:58`), and four comment-only mentions (`zimmProductName`, `theme/index.test.tsx`, `theme/components/index.ts`'s recipe registration, `productInfo.ts`'s comment). `grep -rn "isLive"` across `overrides/` finds it only inside `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` and its own test file — the prop has no consumer anywhere yet.

### 6. Accessibility — CLEAN, this is the crux of the change, extensively verified

Read every assertion in both the pre-existing and new tests (not trusted "12 tests passed"):
- `"announces the price through a polite atomic live region"` (loaded, default) — asserts `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"`, and single-node identity. Unmodified, still passes.
- `"live region stays in the AT and preserves element identity across the loading transition"` (loading, default) — asserts `aria-live` present, node identity preserved across rerender. Unmodified, still passes.
- New test 1 (`isLive={false}`, loaded) — asserts both attributes absent AND `container.querySelectorAll('[aria-live]')` has length 0.
- New test 2 (`isLive={false}` + `isLoading={true}`) — same assertions on the skeleton branch's separate JSX call site.

**Falsification (both mutations run against the real file, then reverted and verified byte-identical via `diff`):**

- **Mutation 1** — hardcoded `liveRegionProps` to always return both attributes, ignoring `isLive`. Result: exactly the 2 new tests failed (`toHaveAttribute('aria-live')` received `"polite"` when expecting absent), all 10 others stayed green. Proves the new tests are real, not tautological.
- **Mutation 2** — flipped the default to `isLive = false` without touching any call site. Result: 3 pre-existing tests failed — `"announces the price through a polite atomic live region"`, `"live region remains a single element in the sale variant"`, and `"live region stays in the AT and preserves element identity across the loading transition"` (all received `null`/length-0 instead of the expected attribute/count). This is stronger evidence than the brief asked for: it shows the default is protected by three tests, not just the two named in the task, and both the loaded-path and loading-path defaults are independently guarded.

Full suite re-run after both reverts: 49 files / 738 tests, byte-identical `diff` against the pre-mutation backup, `git diff --stat` matching the original numbers exactly (19 insertions / 3 deletions in `index.tsx`). No stray mutation artifacts left in the tree.

TypeScript narrowing: `liveRegionProps: { 'aria-live'?: 'polite'; 'aria-atomic'?: 'true' }` — confirmed literal-typed, not widened to `string`, and compiles clean against `chakra.p`'s `AriaAttributes` (`Booleanish = boolean | 'true' | 'false'`). No prior in-repo precedent exists for this exact "computed ARIA-attribute object" pattern (grepped for `'aria-live'`/`'aria-atomic'`/`Booleanish` outside this file — only test-assertion matches turned up), so this is a new but sound pattern, not a departure from an established one.

### 7. Against the ticket — ACs satisfied; one gap in verifiable scope

All 5 numbered "Required verification" items and the "Also check" item are satisfied per above. I could not find an SFCC-236 spec in `.docs/` (grepped the whole `.docs/` tree, zero matches) or in `sprintScope.md` to cross-check the `isLive` design decision against a written requirement — the only documentation of intent is the code's own comments (which are internally consistent and plausible given the branch name `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`). Flagging this as unverifiable rather than assuming the comments are an accurate proxy for a real ticket AC.

### 8. Intra-step DRY — CLEAN, not a UNIFORM finding

The ARIA attribute names/values (`'aria-live'`, `'polite'`, `'aria-atomic'`, `'true'`) appear in both `index.tsx` and `index.test.tsx`, but these are web-platform-standard literal strings being asserted against rendered DOM output, not project-authored design/config values of the kind `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts` exists to deduplicate. No shared-source violation here.

### 9. Visual checkpoint brief — DROPPED (vacuous)

This change alters zero rendered pixels in the default path (confirmed: same JSX structure, same attribute values when `isLive=true`, only the mechanism changed from static literals to a spread) and the `isLive={false}` path only removes non-visual ARIA attributes. There is no rendered-output delta for Marcel to check in DevTools — a table would be padding.

### 10. React logic correctness — DROPPED (vacuous)

`ZimmProductPrice` has no `useState`/`useEffect`/derived state at all — pure prop→JSX mapping. Nothing for this angle to check.

---

## What I tried to falsify

- Attacked the two new tests directly by making the code ignore `isLive` entirely (hardcoding both attributes on). Both tests failed as expected, isolated to exactly those two — survived.
- Attacked the *existing* default-behaviour tests by flipping the default to `false` with no call-site change. Three pre-existing tests failed, proving they weren't passing by coincidence — survived.
- Grepped the entire repository (not just `overrides/`) for every reference to `ZimmProductPrice` and `isLive` to rule out an undiscovered second consumer that might pass `isLive` or otherwise be affected — none found.
- Re-read the full current file top-to-bottom (not just diff hunks) to rule out a silent reorder of Was/Now formatting, `variant` computation, `data-testid`, or hook ordering — none found.
- Checked whether the one real consumer's coverage (`zimmProductContent`) mocks or really renders `ZimmProductPrice`, rather than assuming — it renders for real, and its `play` assertions don't touch ARIA, so genuinely unaffected.
- Ran the full 738-test suite before and after both mutations (and after final revert) rather than trusting a scoped-folder run alone.

## What I could not verify

- No SFCC-236 written spec exists in `.docs/` to check the `isLive` design decision against a formal AC — only the task prompt and the code's own comments describe intent. Noted, not assumed away.
- Whether the eventual PLP/card component that this prop is presumably built for (per the branch name and the code comment's "reused inside a grid of many cards" rationale) will actually pass `isLive={false}` — that component doesn't exist in the repo yet, so this is a forward-looking dependency, not something checkable from this step. Worth a later-step check that the eventual consumer actually wires it up, since an unconsumed prop silently defeats its own purpose.
